strategy.reproducing_test:
def test_splitting_with_missing_values():
    # Non regression test for https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/32178
    X = (
        np.vstack([[0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2]])
        .swapaxes(0, 1)
        .astype(float)
    )
    y = [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1]
    X[X == 0] = np.nan

    for i in range(20):
        tree = DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, random_state=i).fit(X, y)
        assert_array_equal(tree.tree_.impurity, np.array([0.25, 0.0, 0.0]))
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (scikit-learn at commit b1b01a1611e1), running the test `test_splitting_with_missing_values` via the given pytest command must FAIL (at least one of the 20 random_state fits produces `tree.tree_.impurity != [0.25, 0.0, 0.0]`, e.g. `[0.25, 0.1875, 0.1875]`). On the fixed revision (the version containing the PR#32351 fix), the same test must PASS (all 20 random_state fits yield `tree.tree_.impurity == [0.25, 0.0, 0.0]`).
strategy.numerical_probe: The assertion uses an exact array equality (`assert_array_equal`) on `tree.tree_.impurity` with `np.array([0.25, 0.0, 0.0])`. The buggy behavior manifests as impurity being `[0.25, 0.1875, 0.1875]` for at least one of the random_state values within i=0..19.
